name: Kisspeptin

lead: Kisspeptin is a natural signalling peptide that tells the hypothalamus to release GnRH, which drives LH and testosterone. Its fragment kisspeptin-10 is sold as a research peptide, and testosterone-therapy forums discuss it as an alternative to hCG or gonadorelin for keeping the testes active and aiding recovery after cycles, helping maintain muscle, fullness and libido.

It binds KISS1R on GnRH neurons, increasing GnRH pulses and thereby LH and FSH from the pituitary; in men, LH stimulates testicular testosterone production. Academic trials show it raises LH in volunteers, but none tests the forum use or appearance outcomes.

paras: Forum users describe it as a research peptide used alongside testosterone replacement or after a steroid cycle, in place of hCG, usually under clinician or self-directed protocols that vary widely.

It has no approved indication, and products are unregulated research chemicals. Long-term effects of repeated self-administration have not been established in the cited trials, and effects on appearance are untested.

angle.text: Kisspeptin-10 is a hypothalamic peptide that triggers LH release, and TRT users discuss it as an hCG alternative to keep the testes producing testosterone and to aid post-cycle recovery. Academic trials show it raises LH in volunteers; use alongside TRT has not been tested.

lead: Kisspeptins are a family of neuropeptides encoded by the KISS1 gene. They act on the receptor KISS1R (GPR54) on gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) neurons in the hypothalamus, which makes them a key upstream signal for luteinizing hormone (LH), follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) and, in men, testosterone [1][2]. The shortest fully active fragment, kisspeptin-10, and the longer kisspeptin-54 have both been given to people in research settings [3][4].

In testosterone-therapy and bodybuilding forums, kisspeptin-10 is discussed as a way to keep the testes signalling during testosterone replacement or after a steroid cycle, as an alternative to hCG or gonadorelin [5][6][7]. This is an off-label, non-approved use of a research peptide; no kisspeptin product is an approved medicine.

Human studies of kisspeptin are real but small and are conducted by academic endocrinology groups. They show it raises gonadotropins in healthy volunteers and some patients with reproductive disorders [8][9][10]. No trial found here has tested it for muscle, physique or other appearance outcomes.
infobox: KISS1 identified 1996 as a melanoma metastasis suppressor; peptides described 2001 [3][11]
Research peptide; not an approved drug

paras: The peptides derive from the KISS1 gene product and share a C-terminal RF-amide motif; they were first isolated from human placenta and shown to activate the orphan receptor GPR54 [3]. Kisspeptin was named after the chocolate Kisses of Hershey, Pennsylvania, where the gene was found, according to Grokipedia [11].

Kisspeptin stimulates GnRH release directly through GPR54 [1][12]. Inactivating mutations in the receptor cause hypogonadotropic hypogonadism in people, and kisspeptin signalling is regarded as a gatekeeper of puberty [13][2][14]. Neurons in the arcuate nucleus that co-express kisspeptin, neurokinin B and dynorphin shape GnRH pulses [15][16]. Energy balance and stress modulate these neurons [17][18].

On T Nation, users on testosterone replacement describe rotating kisspeptin-10 with gonadorelin because they cannot tolerate hCG [5], or using it during post-cycle recovery with clomiphene [19]. Others describe it as a possible hCG substitute with its own drawbacks, or as something that keeps the testes "alive" without being optimal [20][7]. One user claims it avoids the desensitisation seen with gonadorelin [6]. Posters report using it alongside growth-hormone secretagogue blends for libido [21]. These are individual reports, not controlled observations.

A randomized trial found that intranasal kisspeptin rapidly raised gonadotropin levels in humans [8]. A single kisspeptin-54 injection temporarily increased LH pulsatility in healthy women [4]. A 2025 randomized trial reported that kisspeptin stimulated reproductive hormones without affecting anxiety [9], and a randomized trial examined its acute effects on bone metabolism in healthy men.

Registered trials have tested kisspeptin in infertility and IVF triggering [22], hypothalamic amenorrhea and hypogonadotropic hypogonadism [23][24][25], and as a diagnostic probe of GnRH function [26][10]. These studies are in patients or volunteers and none targets muscle building or testosterone-therapy co-use in men.

The human studies above were conducted under research oversight; the cited abstracts do not establish long-term safety of repeated self-administration. Kisspeptin has no approved medical indication and products sold online are marketed as research peptides, with purity and identity not verified by regulators.
